Key Research Thinking Patterns: Two-Stage Data Curation and Filtering: Implementing sequential deep learning pipelines to isolate high-quality training data from noisy web-sourced datasets, specifically using ResNet-50 with elevated SoftMax thresholds to achieve >98% positive predictive value and significantly reduce false positives in retinal image selection.

Synthetic Data Augmentation via Lesion Projection: Generating realistic training samples by extracting diseased regions from annotated datasets (e.g., IDRiD) and projecting them onto healthy fundus images, thereby overcoming data scarcity and improving classification accuracy by 7.4% compared to models trained on original data alone.

Joint Segmentation-Classification Architectures: Designing unified hybrid models (J-Net) that integrate U-Net segmentation with binary classification heads to perform simultaneous lesion delineation and disease diagnosis, demonstrating superior accuracy (up to 0.95) and data efficiency compared to independent single-task models.

Hybrid Morphological-Deep Learning Integration: Combining mathematical morphology operations (erosion, dilation, residual extraction) with lightweight neural networks (MCNN) and ensemble classifiers (Random Forest, ELM) to enhance feature extraction and diagnostic performance on limited datasets, achieving competitive AUC scores without heavy computational overhead.
Summary Description: Sanjana Mudduluru specializes in Medical Imaging Informatics and Computer-Aided Diagnosis, focusing on deep learning solutions for ophthalmology and dermatology. The researcher addresses critical challenges in medical AI, including data scarcity and noise, through innovative methodologies such as synthetic data generation via lesion projection and two-stage filtering pipelines. Key technical contributions include the development of hybrid architectures like J-Net for joint segmentation-classification and Morphological-Convolutional Neural Networks (MCNN) for efficient glaucoma detection. By leveraging transfer learning with models like ResNet-50 and VGG16, and employing rigorous validation strategies, the research significantly improves diagnostic accuracy and robustness in automated disease detection systems.
